edits.reason: UNSUPPORTED: not in the NHS side-effects excerpt or the pre-patch record.

edits.match: Stopping suddenly after long use carries a high risk that gout will return or worsen, so a doctor reduces the dose slowly if it has to be withdrawn
edits.replacement: Stopping treatment allows uric acid to build up again so that gout returns, so it is not stopped without medical advice
edits.reason: UNSAFE: 'a doctor reduces the dose slowly' is a dose-adjustment instruction with no source (allopurinol is not tapered); 'high risk' overstated.

edits.match: Started low and increased gradually: US information advises increases no more often than weekly, and the NHS that the dose is raised only if the uric acid level has not fallen far enough
edits.replacement: Started at a low dose and increased gradually, because raising the dose too quickly increases the risk of serious skin reactions
edits.reason: UNSAFE: 'increases no more often than weekly' is a dose-adjustment frequency not in the pre-patch record (which says every few weeks) and not in the NHS source; replacement is supported by the NHS statement that Stevens-Johnson syndrome is more likely when the dose is increased too quickly.
